When `considerContextUntrusted` is true (i.e., "Treat context as sensitive from the start of chat" is enabled), `evaluateIfContextIsTrusted` was returning early with empty `toolResultUpdates: {}`, which bypassed ALL Tool Result Policy evaluation — including `block_always` policies.

This meant that raw tool results were sent to the LLM even when they matched a blocked policy.

## Root Cause

In `platform/backend/src/guardrails/trusted-data.ts`, when `considerContextUntrusted` was true, the function returned early before reaching the policy evaluation loop, returning empty `toolResultUpdates`.

## Fix

Instead of returning early, the function now:
1. Sets `hasUntrustedData = true` and `unsafeContextBoundary` (preserving the preexisting_untrusted boundary)
2. Continues to the normal policy evaluation loop
3. Blocked/sanitized tool results are properly evaluated and replaced

Also fixes a secondary bug where the "no tool calls" early return hardcoded `contextIsTrusted: true` instead of `!hasUntrustedData`.

## Testing

- Added regression test: "applies blocked Tool Result Policies even when context starts untrusted"

## Note

I cannot open a PR directly against archestra-ai/archestra due to the prior-contributors restriction. Maintainers can review the diff and cherry-pick, or add my username to EXTERNAL_CONTRIBUTORS.md.

This PR implements filter persistence across page navigations in the Archestra frontend.

### Problem
Filters (scope, teamIds, authorIds, labels) are stored in URL search params, which are page-specific. When navigating between pages (e.g., agents list → agent detail → back), all filter state is lost.

### Solution
1. **New: `FilterPersistenceContext`** - A React Context that stores filter state globally and syncs with `localStorage`.

2. **New: `usePageFilterSync` hook** - Syncs URL params with the global context.

### Files Added
- `platform/frontend/src/lib/contexts/filter-persistence-context.tsx`
- `platform/frontend/src/lib/hooks/use-filter-persistence.ts`

### Next Steps
- Integrate context into `AgentScopeFilter` component
- Integrate context into `LabelSelect` component
- Wrap root layout with `FilterPersistenceProvider`
- Test cross-page navigation

- New `McpServerModel.purge()` hard-deletes where a tombstone must not exist: rollback of a failed install and app-backing servers. Catalog deletion soft-deletes its installs (purging any app backing caught in the cascade), and `catalog_id` is nullable for tombstones only.
- The runtime orphan sweep now tears down deployments, services, secrets, and managed network policies left behind when a tombstoned install's delete-time teardown failed (e.g. cluster unreachable at uninstall).

## Why

Uninstalls previously hard-deleted the row, leaving audit-log entries pointing at entities that no longer resolve. Tombstoning keeps audit history intact while everything the install owned is still destroyed at uninstall time — tombstones are never restorable.

## Testing

- Backend + frontend `pnpm type-check`
- Backend unit/integration tests across all touched files (429 tests): model soft-delete suite (tombstone hiding, secret teardown, reinstall not blocked), catalog delete cascade with app-backing purge backstop, route `status=deleted` listing + permission 403, orphan sweep incl. legacy deployment-name service truncation, and tool-health ranking with a tombstoned install

soft-delete skills","body":"## What

Skills now soft-delete (`deleted_at`) instead of hard-deleting, matching agents and apps. Delete-only scope — no restore flow.

- `skills` converts to `softDeletablePgTable`; both partial name-uniqueness indexes gain a `deleted_at IS NULL` predicate so a deleted skill frees its name (indexes rebuilt transactionally in the migration, with the linter suppression rationale in the file header)
- `SkillModel` read paths filter deleted rows (org listings, `findById`/`findByIds`, name lookups, import-collision checks, sync due-scan); `updateWithFiles`, sync bookkeeping, and usage counters guard their writes the same way; `delete()` uses the shared `softDelete` helper
- Deleting a built-in skill becomes a durable opt-out: `findBuiltIn` deliberately includes soft-deleted rows so the startup seeder sees and skips them — previously the seeder resurrected a deleted built-in on every boot (pre-existing bug)
- Soft-deleted synced skills no longer block GitHub PAT / App config deletion and drop out of the sync due-scan
- Share-link listings and marketplace materialization exclude deleted skills; instance usage counts active skills only
- `findByIdForAudit` keeps returning deleted rows so audit snapshots stay intact; the sandbox revocation gate now fails closed via the filtered `findById`

## Why

Hard deletion destroyed a skill's versions, files, and junction rows the moment it was removed, and made built-in removal impossible (the seeder recreated it by `source_ref` on the next boot). Soft deletion preserves history for audit, keeps name-uniqueness semantics via the partial indexes, and brings skills in line with how agents and apps already behave.

## Testing

- 11 new tests: soft-delete model semantics (hidden reads, idempotent delete, name freeing, audit exception), seeder durable opt-out, share-link exclusion, PAT deletion unblocking, and route-level list/404/name-reuse behavior
- Skill-adjacent sweep green: ~1,690 tests across model, route, seed, archestra-mcp-server, task-queue, and middleware suites
- `type-check`, `lint`, `knip` (dev + production), `drizzle-kit check`, and `check:migrations` all pass

address an app by a custom URL slug","body":"## Summary

An app's shareable URL was its UUID — `/a/7b0839a1-4663-4371-a739-e5dac7f8c33e`. That is the address someone pastes into a doc or sends a colleague, and it is unreadable and unmemorable.

Every app now carries a `slug` derived from its name, so *Sales Dashboard* opens at `/a/sales-dashboard`. Authors can change it under **URL** in app settings. Slugs are unique per organization among non-deleted apps (org-wide rather than per-author, since a URL segment cannot be shared), and deleting an app frees its slug the way it already frees its name. A slug does not follow a rename — it is an address the author controls, so a display-name edit must not silently break links that used it.

Changing a slug stops the old one resolving. `/a/<id>` therefore keeps working permanently as the address no rename breaks, and the model-facing links the app-authoring tools hand back now use the slug with an id fallback.

**The slug addresses the run page only.** `GET /api/apps/:appId` accepts a slug or an id, because a slug in the browser has to resolve server-side somewhere and that is the read the run page already makes. Everything else — every mutating route, the runtime proxy, and the OAuth connector at `POST /api/mcp/app/:appId` — stays uuid-keyed. The connector URI is the RFC 8707 token audience, so a second addressable form would alias it and a rename would invalidate access tokens already living in an external MCP client. `apps.id` also remains the app's isolation key (data-store partition, tool gate, audit), so the run page mounts the runtime on the *resolved* id, never on the URL segment.

Two shapes are refused as slugs beyond the character grammar: a UUID, which would shadow whichever app really owns that id once a segment resolves against `id OR slug`; and `catalog`, which the static `/a/catalog/[catalogId]` route already owns, so an app claiming it would be permanently unreachable. Existing apps are backfilled from their names under the same guards.

soft-delete projects and retain their chats, files, and schedules","body":"## What

Deleting a project now stamps `deleted_at` instead of removing the row. One `belongsToLiveProject` predicate hides everything the project owns:

- **Chats** disappear from the sidebar, by-id reads, mutations, share links, and the browser-stream authorizer. Previously they were detached (`project_id` → NULL) and survived as ordinary conversations.
- **Files** and their stored bytes are retained instead of cascade-deleted; the external-bytes purge on delete is gone.
- **Scheduled tasks** stop firing and drop out of listings, run-now included (404 even for the trigger's owner).

Deleting a user soft-deletes the projects they own first. `projects.user_id` and `files.user_id` move from `ON DELETE CASCADE` to `SET NULL` so the rows survive ownerless. The display name is freed for reuse (the unique index is now partial on `deleted_at IS NULL`) while the slug stays claimed, so retained bytes stay addressable in their existing folder.

## Why

Project deletion was irreversible and took real work with it: files, stored bytes, and scheduled tasks were purged by FK cascade with no recovery path, while the chats it detached became orphans no longer findable by project. Retention-first makes an accidental delete an operator-recoverable event instead of a final one, and keeps a project's chats grouped with it rather than scattering them.

## How

`belongsToLiveProject(projectIdColumn)` in `models/project.ts` is the single predicate for every table carrying a `project_id` FK, so hiding is uniform across list, by-id, mutate, and delete paths instead of per-call-site. Paths that already resolve a project first — `ProjectModel.findById`, `resolveProjectFileScope`, `FileStore.authorizedFile` — inherit the guard for free.

It is applied to the hard-delete path too: without it, the owner of a hidden chat could still destroy the retained row through a remembered id while every read of it 404s.

There is no restore endpoint and no purge job — recovery is a manual `restore()` (`database/soft-delete.ts`).

## Testing

- Backend tests for the affected areas — 32 tests across `project`, `user`, `project-pin`, `delete.project.route`, plus two new route tests (`deleted-project.conversation.route`, `run-now.schedule-trigger.route`). All pass.
- `pnpm type-check` — clean across the workspace.
- `pnpm knip` (dev + production) — clean.
- `biome check` on the changed files — clean.
- Not yet run: the full backend suite (running now) and e2e. Draft until those are green.

The platform 1.3.0 release ([run 28805632240](https://github.com/archestra-ai/archestra/actions/runs/28805632240)) failed **three consecutive attempts** on the `Build platform (linux/arm64)` job, each time with:

```
skopeo copy ... registry.dagger.io/engine:v0.21.5
fatal msg="... fetching blob: received unexpected HTTP status: 504 Gateway Timeout"
```

Each attempt failed on a *different* small blob (16:16, 16:31, 16:38 UTC), i.e. registry.dagger.io is intermittently 504ing on individual blob fetches. The engine image has ~100 layers and `skopeo copy` aborts on the first failed fetch, so even a 1–2% registry error rate reliably kills the build.

## Fix

Add `--retry-times 5` to the `skopeo copy` that pre-bakes the Dagger engine tarball, so transient blob-fetch failures are retried instead of fatal.

redesign the model-provider connection onboarding","body":"## What

- Two-door credential setup on Model Providers: "Paste an API key" vs "Use a subscription" (ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot), with an onboarding variant of the add-key form, a post-create "Connected — key verified" screen listing discovered models, and the Subscriptions panel always leading the page.
- Subscription device-flow sign-in is now two explicit steps: the code + instructions render first (auto-fetched when a dialog shows a single provider), and the provider page opens only on a dedicated button click — never automatically.
- Chat: the amber "Sign in to X" banner is replaced by a compact "Sign in" chip on the composer model pill (all toolbar states); Enter on an unconnected subscription opens the sign-in dialog instead of firing a send that dies at the provider.
- Subscription-aware default-model resolution: an agent/org default backed by a ChatGPT subscription is held per-user (model kept, key dropped) for viewers who don't own the credential, instead of being silently swapped to an org key. The agents API exposes `llmProviderRequiresPerUserCredential`, including decrypt-based detection of ChatGPT-subscription keys riding the `openai` provider.
- Personal subscription keys are self-service (owner-checked update/delete), edit is rename-only for subscriptions, and removal is phrased as "Disconnect".

## Why

Connecting a subscription was buried inside the OpenAI key form's auth tabs, and chat silently substituted another credential when the viewer hadn't connected their own subscription — sends failed at the provider and who pays could change invisibly. This makes subscriptions first-class: a discoverable connect flow, explicit sign-in affordances, and per-user resolution that never silently swaps keys.

## Testing

- Unit: targeted vitest across the touched frontend suites (135 tests) and backend agent-model tests; `biome check` and `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Live verification on the dev stack with two accounts (admin + member): the backend per-user flag is correct for both viewers, and the resolver replayed against each account's real API payloads holds subscription-backed defaults per-user with no org-key swap.
- e2e: the `use-subscription` Playwright spec was updated for the new flow but not run locally.

render LaTeX math in chat responses","body":"## Summary

- Renders LaTeX in chat replies. Wires the `@streamdown/math` plugin (remark-math + rehype-katex) into `Response` and imports KaTeX's stylesheet in `globals.css` — the plugin only reports the path via `getStyles()`, it never injects it, so without the `@import` formulas collapse into unpositioned spans.
- `singleDollarTextMath` stays off (the plugin default) so prices in prose are not read as math. Two preprocessing passes rewrite what models actually emit into the `$$` form remark-math parses:
  - `preprocess-latex.ts` (vendored from LibreChat, MIT) detects currency *positively* — a `$` that introduces digits — escapes it, then promotes every `$…$` still standing. Prices are the identifiable case; math is the remainder.
  - `normalize-math.ts` rewrites `\(…\)` / `\[…\]`. This has to run on the raw string: CommonMark backslash-escapes ASCII punctuation, so `\( x \)` is already the plain text `( x )` by the time an mdast tree exists and no remark/rehype plugin can recover it.
- Both passes protect code spans and fences, including the unclosed fence that routinely exists mid-stream. Upstream drops that case, which leaves a half-arrived code block getting rewritten while it streams.
- Display math only earns its own lines when it already owns an unindented one. The injected newlines land at column 0, so applying it to an indented list-item continuation would drop the body out of the list and swallow whatever follows.
- `katex` is pinned `^0.16.27` to match the version `@streamdown/math` → `rehype-katex` actually renders with. The constraint is recorded next to the `@import` because a mismatch fails silently — nothing in the build or the tests compares the stylesheet to the renderer.

## Tests

- `vitest run src/components/ai-elements/` — 86 passed. `normalize-math.test.ts` and `preprocess-latex.test.ts` cover the rewrites directly; the new `response.test.ts` block renders through real Streamdown, so it also pins that the plugin is wired up, that its rehype stage survives rehype-harden, and that display vs inline is preserved.
- `pnpm build` — shipped CSS reports `katex-version: 0.16.28`, matching the renderer; all 60 KaTeX fonts emit with rebased URLs.
- `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm knip` — clean.

## Known limitation

Two unescaped `$` on one line still pair into math, because the currency pass only recognises *prefix* amounts. Unbackticked shell prose regresses:

```
Set $HOME and $PATH before running.   ->   Set $$HOME and $$PATH before running.
```

"HOME and " then renders as a formula. Postfix currency (`5$ or 10$`) hits the same path. Needs a constraint on `SINGLE_DOLLAR_REGEX`'s body rather than a smarter currency rule; deliberately not attempted here. Draft until this is settled.

Smaller, lower-impact edges left open: an *unpaired* `\[` can let bracket math span a fenced block (normal paired shapes are unaffected), `$a$$b$` with no space between spans corrupts both, and `findCodeBlockRegions` does not implement CommonMark's backtick-run length matching or paragraph boundary — that one fails toward skipping processing rather than corrupting.

No `docs/pages/` change: `platform-chat.md` documents no markdown rendering at all today (tables, code copy/download and the link-safety dialog are equally undocumented), so a math section would be the first of its kind. Happy to add one if reviewers would rather it land with the feature.

add the creator to the team they create, as its admin","body":"## Why

Creating a team set `created_by` but never wrote a `team_member` row. Every team-scoped check reads membership rather than that column, so the creator landed outside their own team.

For a caller holding `team:create` without organization-level `team:update`, that means creating a team and being immediately locked out of it:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/teams/:id` (own team) | 404 | 200 |
| `POST /api/teams/:id/members` | 403 | 200 |
| `GET /api/teams?mine=true` | team absent | team present |

`canReadTeam` resolves to `isUserInTeam` and `canManageTeamMembers` to `isUserTeamAdmin`, so with no membership row the only way to touch a team you just made was an organization-wide permission — which is exactly the permission a scoped team creator doesn't have.

## What changed

`TeamModel.create` now inserts the creator as a team **admin**, in the same transaction as the team row, so a team is never persisted without one.

Admin rather than member because whoever creates a team is the one expected to fill it — that is what restores access without granting anything organization-wide. `synced_from_sso` stays `false`, so SSO team sync treats it as a manual membership and never removes it.

## Blast radius

Only teams created through `TeamModel.create` are affected: the REST route, the `create_team` tool, and the seed script — all of which pass the acting user as `created_by`. It is the only production insert into `teams`, and no SSO or import path creates teams, so nothing gains a member it shouldn't have.

Two interactions worth noting, both already safe:

- `POST /api/teams/:id/members` returns a 409 for an existing member rather than colliding on the unique `(team_id, user_id)` index.
- The team dialog only renders member management once the team exists, so a staged member change cannot race the new row on create.

## Behavior changes

- A newly created team reports `memberCount: 1` instead of `0`, and `TeamModel.create` returns that member rather than `[]`.
- The creator can now read, manage, and see their own team without organization-level team permissions.

## Tests

- Model: the creator is persisted as an admin with `syncedFromSso: false`, is returned in `members`, and appears in `getUserAdminTeamIds` / `getUserTeamIds`.
- Route: with `team: ["update"]` withheld — so being the team's admin is the only route to access — the creator can read the team, add a member, and see it under `?mine=true`. Verified all three fail without the fix, returning exactly the reported 404 / 403 / absent.
- Updated the two `memberCount` assertions that pinned the old counts, and replaced an index-based `members[0]` lookup with one keyed on the user, since that list now holds two rows.

Full `src/routes`, `src/services`, `src/models`, and `src/archestra-mcp-server` sweep compared against a clean `main` baseline: the failing set is identical (21 files, all pre-existing and app-suite related), with none added or removed. `type-check`, `lint`, and `knip` (dev + production) pass.

## Docs

Added a line to the Team Roles section of Access Control noting that the creator joins as the team's first admin.

price Bedrock models from the AWS Price List","body":"Bedrock prices came from a community registry that is wrong in two ways.

It carries no entry for **23 of 94** models — retired ones like Claude 3 Sonnet and Llama 3.2, and non-chat ones like the Titan embeddings — so each fell back to a fabricated $50/M, or $30/M when the id read as small. Measured against real rates the errors ran from 12× to 500×: `us.meta.llama3-2-1b-instruct` was billed at $50 against $0.10, `us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku` at $30 against $0.25.

It also publishes one price per model, so it cannot express that Bedrock charges 10% more for regional endpoints than global ones. Every `us.`/`eu.`/`apac.` profile was therefore priced at the global rate — Claude Sonnet 4.5 at $3.00 where AWS charges $3.30.

Neither is cosmetic: these figures flow into recorded interaction cost, cost statistics, optimization-rule savings and token-cost limits.

AWS publishes its own prices at a public endpoint needing no credentials, covering the retired models and distinguishing the two endpoint tiers. Those prices are transcribed into a small committed artifact and take precedence over the registry for Bedrock, which remains the fallback. After this, Bedrock models without a real price drop from 23 to 4 — a reranker and three video-model variants, none of which is billed per token.

The artifact records what AWS charges rather than how to fetch it, so nothing new runs at sync time and the tests stay hermetic. Refreshing means re-reading the two offer documents named in the resolver. Three rules govern the transcription and each is easy to get wrong: a price is published per 1K *or* per 1M tokens with both forms inside one document; `batch`, `flex` and `priority` SKUs sit beside the standard on-demand price; and a suffix on the usage type marks the cheaper global-endpoint price.

Model identity is stated rather than derived, because AWS names a priced model three different ways — `Llama 3.2 90B`, `Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Amazon Bedrock Edition)`, and embeddings under a separate attribute as `TitanEmbeddingsV2-Text-input`. An id that maps to nothing resolves to nothing and falls through; there is no fuzzy matching, because a model priced as the wrong model is worse than one that is visibly unpriced.

Prices only. AWS publishes no token limits, so context windows are unchanged and the models the registry cannot describe keep a null context.

A price now states its own origin, with `aws` joining the price sources. The exception is an application inference profile: its id encodes nothing and the underlying model name is not persisted, so its origin cannot be re-derived after the sync that resolved it, and it continues to report the registry.

switch from Blacksmith to GitHub-hosted runners","body":"## What

Moves all CI off Blacksmith onto GitHub-hosted runners.

- **Runner labels** (27 workflows): every `blacksmith-{2,4,8,16}vcpu-ubuntu-2404` → `ubuntu-24.04`; `blacksmith-16vcpu-ubuntu-2404-arm` → `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (free for public repos).
- **Wrapper actions** renamed and repointed to upstream, same pin-by-SHA convention:
  - `setup-blacksmith-builder` → `setup-docker-builder` (`docker/setup-buildx-action` v4.2.0)
  - `blacksmith-build-push` → `docker-build-push` (`docker/build-push-action` v7.3.0)
  - `github-cache` now wraps `actions/cache` v6.1.0 instead of `useblacksmith/cache` (identical interface)
- **Layer caching**: Blacksmith's sticky disks are gone, so `docker-build-push` defaults to reading the GHA BuildKit cache (`cache-from: type=gha`), and `warm-e2e-build-cache.yml` becomes the single designated writer (`cache-to: type=gha,mode=max`). PR/merge-queue builds read main's cache via GHA branch scoping; ordinary builds don't export, keeping churn in the 10 GB per-repo budget bounded.

## Caveats to be aware of

- **Slower builds**: the 8/16-vCPU Blacksmith jobs (platform image build, e2e legs, multi-arch native builds) now run on 4-vCPU standard runners. If that hurts the merge-queue critical path, GitHub larger runners can be configured org-side and the labels swapped in.
- **Cache eviction**: as documented in `github-cache/action.yml`, CodeQL churns ~11 GB into the 10 GB Actions cache LRU, so warmed entries (image tarballs, Playwright browsers, and now BuildKit layers) can be evicted before the hot path — expect occasional cold builds/restores.
- The MCP server base image build reads `type=gha` but has no warming writer (Blacksmith cached it implicitly); it's a small image, but a follow-up could add it to the warm workflow if it shows up in timings.

## Verification

- All 26 changed YAML files parse.
- Every input passed to the pinned `docker/build-push-action` and `actions/cache` SHAs was checked against those versions' `action.yml` (including `network`, `provenance`, `secrets`, `cache-from`/`cache-to`).
- No `blacksmith`/`useblacksmith` references remain anywhere in `.github/`.

reject inputs that poison a sandbox's replay log","body":"Three input-validation gaps let a value that passes create/update/upload validation but later fails Rust replay conversion get persisted into the append-only `skill_sandbox_replay_events` log, **permanently bricking a conversation's default sandbox** (every later `run_command`/`download_file` fails). Fixed at the **input boundary** so no new poison is persisted; the Rust replay boundary (`validate_snapshot_file_path`) is left unchanged — tightening it would strand already-persisted mounts.

## Fixes
- **Upload/artifact path (B1)**: reject a *terminal* `.` (`/home/sandbox/.` resolves to a directory, so the replayed `base64 -d > <path>` redirect fails forever). Non-terminal `.` (`./x`, `a/./b`) resolves to a regular file and is allowed. Fixed in the TS twin (`resolveArtifactPath`) and Rust (`validate_upload_path`/`validate_artifact_path` via a new `resolves_to_directory` helper), with the mirrored vector tables kept in sync.
- **Skill name (C6)**: reject a name that is `.` or contains `/` or `..` at `parseSkillManifest`, and — the universal chokepoint — at `mountSkill` (`validateSkillMountName`), mirroring the Rust `skill_root_path` boundary. The mount-side check closes a bypass where a white-label app name is spliced into a built-in skill name without going through the parser.
- **Resource path (C7)**: reject absolute, `..`, and terminal empty/`.` segments via a shared `isSafeSkillResourcePath` predicate, applied by both `SkillFileInputSchema` and the GitHub importer (which previously skipped the schema).

## Scope
Forward-only: existing rows with poison names/paths, the app-name→built-in-skill-name normalization, and a pre-existing trailing-slash *artifact-download* friendliness gap (non-poisoning) are tracked as follow-ups.

## Validation
`pnpm type-check`, `cargo test -p sandbox_core`, `cargo clippy -p sandbox_core --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the affected backend suites (parser, create-skill route, skill-sandbox path vectors + mount-name, github-import) all pass; biome clean.

## Review
Two adversarial review rounds. Round 1 caught an over-rejection regression (rejecting *every* `.` segment, now narrowed to terminal) and two persistence bypasses (built-in white-label name, GitHub import paths), all fixed. Round 2 confirmed no remaining security blocker.

give apps a per-viewer file store via the built-in file tools","body":"## What

MCP apps can now use the built-in file tools — `search_files`, `read_file`, `save_file`, `edit_file`, `delete_file`, plus `upload_file` / `download_file` — called from app HTML through `archestra.tools.call`. `run_command` stays out: an app is a UI surface, not an execution environment.

The store is scoped to the **(app, viewer)** pair and is the same store on every app surface — inline in chat, the standalone `/a/<id>` page, and the shareable connector. An app never reaches a chat's or a project's files, and two viewers of one app never see each other's.

No new identity surface: the viewer is already the principal for RBAC, invocation policy, and per-viewer credential resolution, so the tools inherit that model unchanged (`file:manage`, and `sandbox:execute` for the transfer pair). Every predefined role already holds both.

Closes T-567.

## How

- **Namespace.** Nullable `app_id` on `files` and `skill_sandboxes`, each with a partial unique index keyed on it. The orphan index gains `AND app_id IS NULL` — without that, every app write would collide with the headless bucket on `(user_id, filename)`. `fileStore` / `object-store` gain an app scope; store paths nest under `<email>/apps/<appId>`.
- **One availability predicate.** `isAppRuntimeBuiltinAvailable` folds the allowlist and the sandbox flag together, and the gate, the dispatch branch, `tools/list`, and the SDK bootstrap all ask it. The file tools are registered only under the sandbox runtime, so without this the gate would admit a call dispatch could not resolve.
- **App-only visibility.** The file tools are marked `visibility: ["app"]` in `tools/list`, same rationale as `llm_complete`: an embedding host's model must not roam the viewer's files, while the app's own code still calls them.
- **One sandbox per app.** `resolveTarget` resolves the `(org, viewer, app)` default for every sandbox-backed call and refuses an explicit `target`, so a second instance cannot appear.

## Two adjacent fixes

- `sandboxConversationInScope` returned `true` for any conversation-less, isolation-less caller. With the transfer tools reachable from apps, `target: {id}` would have reached another app's (or a headless run's) sandbox for the same user. Now an app's sandbox matches only its own app, in both directions.
- `preview_app_tool`'s `app-builtin` branch was unreachable — a pre-gate rejection ran before the gate was consulted, making the gate's own verdict dead code. Built-ins are now previewable and exercise the same namespace the running app sees. `read_file` results are redacted from audit rows rather than storing a second copy of the bytes.

## Testing

`type-check`, `biome`, `knip`, and the migration linter are clean (0 errors; the FK/index warnings are covered by a documented pragma — both `app_id` columns are NULL on every existing row, so the validations and new uniques match nothing).

Backend suites: **605 tests** across the touched areas, plus 566 in `shared`. New coverage pins the allowlist with the flag on *and* off, the cross-app / cross-viewer isolation matrix through the route, the explicit-`target` refusal, and the one-sandbox-per-(app, viewer) invariant under concurrent creation.

Verified live on a dev stack against real Postgres: save→read→search roundtrip; two apps holding the same filename with different contents, neither visible to the other; `scaffold_app` still refused; explicit `target` refused; the row landing app-scoped with null conversation/project; the audit row carrying the redaction marker; the standalone page serving 200.

One gap, stated plainly: the flag-**off** path was verified by unit test but not live — the stack's backend carries `ARCHESTRA_CODE_RUNTIME_ENABLED=true` in its process env from Tilt, and that cannot be flipped without a full `tilt down && tilt up`.

## Note for review

#6531 shipped a different take on this (apps reading the *embedding chat's* files, assignable, `conversationId` threaded from the React host) and was reverted the next day by #6630 with no recorded reason. This design deliberately avoids both of those aspects — the namespace is the app's own, and there is no assignment machinery — but if the revert had a motive that still applies here, it would be worth hearing before merge.

suggest host.docker.internal when localhost connection fails","body":"## Summary
When an Ollama server is configured with a localhost URL (e.g., http://localhost:11434/v1) and the connection fails (common when Archestra runs inside Docker), the error message now includes a helpful hint recommending the use of http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1.

## Changes
- **platform/backend/src/routes/chat/model-fetchers/ollama.ts**:
  - Added try/catch around the fetch call to detect network-level errors
  - Detect if the base URL contains localhost or 127.0.0.1
  - When connection fails with a localhost URL, throw an error that includes: \If you are running Archestra in Docker, try changing the URL to http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1\

## Problem
Issue #4286 reports two problems:
1. ~~Ollama doesn't work without dummy API key~~ (tracked separately)
2. When Archestra runs in Docker and Ollama is on the host localhost, the connection fails silently with no guidance

## Solution

  <script>
    let currentUser = null;
    let allPrs = []; // holds the fetched list
    let filteredPrs = []; // holds the filtered list for rendering
    let activePreset = 'authored';
    let isFetching = false;

    // Wait for SDK to be ready
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", async () => {
      await window.archestra?.ready;
      lucide.createIcons();
      
      try {
        currentUser = await window.archestra.tools.call('github__get_me');
        if (currentUser && currentUser.login) {
          document.getElementById('username').innerText = currentUser.login;
          if (currentUser.avatar_url) {
            document.getElementById('user-avatar').src = currentUser.avatar_url;
            document.getElementById('user-avatar').classList.remove('hidden');
          }
        }
      } catch (err) {
        console.error("Failed to fetch user profile:", err);
        if (err.code === 'auth_required') {
          showAuthRequired(err);
          return;
        }
        document.getElementById('username').innerText = "GitHub disconnected";
      }

      // Initialize with default preset
      await loadPreset(activePreset);
    });

    function showAuthRequired(err) {
      const container = document.getElementById('main-content');
      container.innerHTML = `
        <div class="max-w-md mx-auto my-12 p-8 bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900 rounded-xl shadow-md border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800 text-center">
          <div class="inline-flex p-3 bg-amber-50 dark:bg-amber-950/30 rounded-full text-amber-600 dark:text-amber-400 mb-4">
            <svg class="w-8 h-8" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor">
              <path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M12 9v2m0 4h.01m-6.938 4h13.856c1.54 0 2.502-1.667 1.732-3L13.732 4c-.77-1.333-2.694-1.333-3.464 0L3.34 16c-.77 1.333.192 3 1.732 3z" />
            </svg>
          </div>
          <h2 class="text-xl font-semibold mb-2">GitHub Connection Required</h2>
          <p class="text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400 text-sm mb-6">${err.message}</p>
          <button onclick="window.archestra.ui.openLink('${err.url}')" class="w-full py-2.5 px-4 bg-zinc-900 text-white dark:bg-white dark:text-zinc-900 rounded-lg text-sm font-semibold hover:bg-zinc-800 dark:hover:bg-zinc-100 transition-all active:scale-95 inline-flex justify-center items-center gap-2 mb-3 cursor-pointer">
            <span>Connect GitHub Account</span>
            <i data-lucide="external-link" class="w-4 h-4"></i>
          </button>
          <button onclick="window.location.reload()" class="w-full py-2 px-4 border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800 text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 rounded-lg text-sm font-semibold hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800 transition-all active:scale-95">
            I connected it, reload page
          </button>
        </div>
      `;
      lucide.createIcons();
    }

    async function changePreset(presetId) {
      if (isFetching) return;
      activePreset = presetId;
      
      // Update UI classes for active state
      const presets = ['authored', 'review-requested', 'my-repos'];
      presets.forEach(p => {
        const el = document.getElementById(`preset-${p}`);
        if (p === presetId) {
          el.className = "w-full flex items-center justify-between px-3 py-2 rounded-lg text-sm font-medium transition-all bg-zinc-900 text-white dark:bg-white dark:text-zinc-900";
        } else {
          el.className = "w-full flex items-center justify-between px-3 py-2 rounded-lg text-sm font-medium transition-all text-zinc-600 hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-400 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800/50";
        }
      });

      // Clear search input on preset change
      document.getElementById('custom-query-input').value = "";

      await loadPreset(presetId);
    }

    async function loadPreset(presetId) {
      if (!currentUser) return;
      const username = currentUser.login;
      let query = "";

      if (presetId === 'authored') {
        query = `is:open is:pr author:${username}`;
      } else if (presetId === 'review-requested') {
        query = `is:open is:pr review-requested:${username}`;
      } else if (presetId === 'my-repos') {
        query = `is:open is:pr user:${username}`;
      }

      await executeSearch(query);
    }

    async function handleCustomQuery(e) {
      e.preventDefault();
      const query = document.getElementById('custom-query-input').value.trim();
      if (!query) return;

      // Deactivate presets visually
      const presets = ['authored', 'review-requested', 'my-repos'];
      presets.forEach(p => {
        const el = document.getElementById(`preset-${p}`);
        el.className = "w-full flex items-center justify-between px-3 py-2 rounded-lg text-sm font-medium transition-all text-zinc-600 hover:bg-zinc-50 dark:text-zinc-400 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800/50";
      });

      await executeSearch(query);
    }

    async function fetchPullRequests() {
      // Re-fetch current query
      if (document.getElementById('custom-query-input').value.trim()) {
        const query = document.getElementById('custom-query-input').value.trim();
        await executeSearch(query);
      } else {
        await loadPreset(activePreset);
      }
    }

    async function executeSearch(query) {
      if (isFetching) return;
      isFetching = true;
      toggleRefreshAnimation(true);
      showLoadingState();

      try {
        const result = await window.archestra.tools.call('github__search_pull_requests', { query });
        allPrs = result.items || [];
        applyLocalFilters();
        updateStats();
      } catch (err) {
        console.error("Error fetching pull requests:", err);
        if (err.code === 'auth_required') {
          showAuthRequired(err);
          return;
        }
        showErrorState(err.message || "An error occurred while fetching PRs.");
      } finally {
        isFetching = false;
        toggleRefreshAnimation(false);
      }
    }

    function toggleRefreshAnimation(animating) {
      const icon = document.getElementById('refresh-icon');
      if (animating) {
        icon.classList.add('animate-spin');
      } else {
        icon.classList.remove('animate-spin');
      }
    }

    function showLoadingState() {
      const container = document.getElementById('queue-container');
      container.innerHTML = `
        <div class="text-center py-20 bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900/40 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800 p-6">
          <div class="inline-block animate-spin rounded-full h-8 w-8 border-4 border-zinc-300 border-t-zinc-900 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:border-t-white mb-4"></div>
          <p class="text-sm font-medium text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400">Contacting GitHub APIs...</p>
          <p class="text-xs text-zinc-400 dark:text-zinc-500 mt-1">Retrieving latest pull requests details.</p>
        </div>
      `;
    }

    function showErrorState(message) {
      const container = document.getElementById('queue-container');
      container.innerHTML = `
        <div class="text-center py-12 bg-red-50 dark:bg-red-950/20 rounded-xl border border-red-200 dark:border-red-900/50 p-6">
          <div class="inline-flex p-3 bg-red-100 dark:bg-red-950/50 rounded-full text-red-600 dark:text-red-400 mb-4">
            <i data-lucide="alert-circle" class="w-8 h-8"></i>
          </div>
          <h3 class="text-lg font-bold text-red-800 dark:text-red-400 mb-1">Search failed</h3>
          <p class="text-sm text-red-600 dark:text-red-400 max-w-md mx-auto">${message}</p>
          <button onclick="fetchPullRequests()" class="mt-4 inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 px-4 py-2 bg-red-600 text-white rounded-lg text-sm font-semibold hover:bg-red-700 active:scale-95 cursor-pointer">
            <i data-lucide="refresh-cw" class="w-4 h-4"></i>
            <span>Retry Connection</span>
          </button>
        </div>
      `;
      lucide.createIcons();
    }

    function getWaitTimeText(dateString) {
      const created = new Date(dateString);
      const now = new Date();
      const diffMs = now - created;
      const diffSec = Math.floor(diffMs / 1000);
      const diffMin = Math.floor(diffSec / 60);
      const diffHour = Math.floor(diffMin / 60);
      const diffDay = Math.floor(diffHour / 24);

      if (diffDay > 0) {
        return `${diffDay} day${diffDay > 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;
      } else if (diffHour > 0) {
        return `${diffHour} hour${diffHour > 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;
      } else if (diffMin > 0) {
        return `${diffMin} min${diffMin > 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;
      } else {
        return `Just now`;
      }
    }

    function getWaitTimeBadgeStyle(dateString) {
      const created = new Date(dateString);
      const now = new Date();
      const diffDays = Math.floor((now - created) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24));

      if (diffDays >= 7) {
        return {
          bg: 'bg-red-50 dark:bg-red-950/20',
          border: 'border-red-200 dark:border-red-900/30',
          text: 'text-red-700 dark:text-red-400',
          dot: 'bg-red-500',
          label: 'Stale (7d+)',
          priority: 1
        };
      } else if (diffDays >= 3) {
        return {
          bg: 'bg-amber-50 dark:bg-amber-950/20',
          border: 'border-amber-200 dark:border-amber-900/30',
          text: 'text-amber-700 dark:text-amber-400',
          dot: 'bg-amber-500',
          label: 'Waiting (3d+)',
          priority: 2
        };
      } else {
        return {
          bg: 'bg-emerald-50 dark:bg-emerald-950/20',
          border: 'border-emerald-200 dark:border-emerald-900/30',
          text: 'text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-400',
          dot: 'bg-emerald-500',
          label: 'Fresh (<3d)',
          priority: 3
        };
      }
    }

    function applyLocalFilters() {
      const searchVal = document.getElementById('local-search-input').value.toLowerCase().trim();
      const sortBy = document.getElementById('sort-order').value;

      // Filter
      filteredPrs = allPrs.filter(pr => {
        const repoName = pr.repository_url ? pr.repository_url.replace("https://api.github.com/repos/", "") : "";
        const titleMatch = pr.title && pr.title.toLowerCase().includes(searchVal);
        const repoMatch = repoName.toLowerCase().includes(searchVal);
        const authorMatch = pr.user && pr.user.login.toLowerCase().includes(searchVal);
        return titleMatch || repoMatch || authorMatch;
      });

      // Sort
      if (sortBy === 'oldest') {
        filteredPrs.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.created_at) - new Date(b.created_at));
      } else {
        filteredPrs.sort((a, b) => new Date(b.created_at) - new Date(a.created_at));
      }

      renderQueue();
    }

    function updateStats() {
      // Total
      document.getElementById('stat-total').innerText = allPrs.length;

      // Stale & Waiting calculations
      let staleCount = 0;
      let actionCount = 0;
      const now = new Date();

      allPrs.forEach(pr => {
        const created = new Date(pr.created_at);
        const diffDays = Math.floor((now - created) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24));
        if (diffDays >= 7) {
          staleCount++;
        }
        if (diffDays >= 3) {
          actionCount++;
        }
      });

      document.getElementById('stat-stale').innerText = staleCount;
      document.getElementById('stat-waiting').innerText = actionCount;

      // Update preset badges if we have them
      const badgeAuthored = document.getElementById('badge-authored');
      const badgeRequested = document.getElementById('badge-requested');
      const badgeRepos = document.getElementById('badge-repos');

      if (activePreset === 'authored') {
        badgeAuthored.innerText = allPrs.length;
        badgeAuthored.classList.remove('hidden');
      } else if (activePreset === 'review-requested') {
        badgeRequested.innerText = allPrs.length;
        badgeRequested.classList.remove('hidden');
      } else if (activePreset === 'my-repos') {
        badgeRepos.innerText = allPrs.length;
        badgeRepos.classList.remove('hidden');
      }
    }

    function renderQueue() {
      const container = document.getElementById('queue-container');
      
      if (filteredPrs.length === 0) {
        container.innerHTML = `
          <div class="text-center py-16 bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900/40 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800 p-6">
            <div class="inline-flex p-3 bg-zinc-100 dark:bg-zinc-800/80 rounded-full text-zinc-400 dark:text-zinc-500 mb-4">
              <i data-lucide="inbox" class="w-8 h-8"></i>
            </div>
            <h3 class="text-lg font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 mb-1">Queue is empty</h3>
            <p class="text-sm text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 max-w-sm mx-auto">No open pull requests found matching the active filters or search parameters.</p>
          </div>
        `;
        lucide.createIcons();
        return;
      }

      let html = '';
      filteredPrs.forEach(pr => {
        const repoName = pr.repository_url ? pr.repository_url.replace("https://api.github.com/repos/", "") : "Unknown repo";
        const waitTimeText = getWaitTimeText(pr.created_at);
        const style = getWaitTimeBadgeStyle(pr.created_at);
        const draftBadge = pr.draft ? `<span class="inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded bg-zinc-100 dark:bg-zinc-800 px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold text-zinc-500">Draft</span>` : '';
        
        // Render labels
        let labelsHtml = '';
        if (pr.labels && pr.labels.length > 0) {
          labelsHtml = pr.labels.map(lbl => {
            const styleString = lbl.color ? `background-color: #${lbl.color}20; color: #${lbl.color}; border: 1px solid #${lbl.color}40;` : '';
            return `<span class="inline-flex items-center px-2 py-0.5 rounded-md text-xs font-medium mr-1.5 mb-1" style="${styleString}">${lbl.name}</span>`;
          }).join('');
        }

        html += `
          <div class="group relative rounded-xl border bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900/50 p-5 shadow-sm transition-all hover:shadow-md dark:border-zinc-800 hover:border-zinc-300 dark:hover:border-zinc-700 flex flex-col md:flex-row md:items-center justify-between gap-4">
            
            <!-- Left content: Info & wait time status -->
            <div class="flex items-start gap-4 flex-1">
              <!-- Visual Age indicator line -->
              <div class="w-1.5 self-stretch rounded-full ${style.dot}"></div>

              <div class="space-y-1.5 flex-1">
                <!-- Repo name and wait badge -->
                <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2 text-xs font-semibold text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400">
                  <span class="font-mono text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300">${repoName}</span>
                  <span class="text-zinc-300 dark:text-zinc-700">•</span>
                  <span class="inline-flex items-center gap-1 px-2.5 py-0.5 rounded-full text-xs font-medium border ${style.bg} ${style.border} ${style.text}">
                    <span class="w-1.5 h-1.5 rounded-full ${style.dot} inline-block"></span>
                    <span>Waiting ${waitTimeText}</span>
                  </span>
                  ${draftBadge}
                </div>

                <!-- Title -->
                <h4 class="text-base font-bold text-zinc-900 dark:text-white group-hover:text-zinc-700 dark:group-hover:text-zinc-300 transition-colors">
                  <a href="javascript:void(0)" onclick="window.archestra.ui.openLink('${pr.html_url}')" class="hover:underline">
                    #${pr.number} ${pr.title}
                  </a>
                </h4>

                <!-- PR labels -->
                <div class="flex flex-wrap pt-1">
                  ${labelsHtml}
                </div>

                <!-- Metadata: author, update date -->
                <div class="flex items-center gap-2 text-xs text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 pt-1">
                  <img class="h-5 w-5 rounded-full border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800" src="${pr.user.avatar_url}" alt="${pr.user.login}" />
                  <span>Opened by <strong class="font-semibold text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300">${pr.user.login}</strong></span>
                  <span>•</span>
                  <span>Last updated ${getWaitTimeText(pr.updated_at)}</span>
                  <span>•</span>
                  <span class="inline-flex items-center gap-1">
                    <i data-lucide="message-square" class="w-3.5 h-3.5"></i>
                    <span>${pr.comments} comments</span>
                  </span>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>

            <!-- Right actions -->
            <div class="flex items-center gap-2 self-end md:self-center">
              <button onclick="window.archestra.ui.openLink('${pr.html_url}')" class="inline-flex h-9 items-center justify-center rounded-lg bg-zinc-900 text-white hover:bg-zinc-800 dark:bg-white dark:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:bg-zinc-100 px-4 text-sm font-semibold transition-all shadow-sm active:scale-95 gap-1.5 cursor-pointer">
                <span>Review</span>
                <i data-lucide="external-link" class="w-4 h-4"></i>
              </button>
            </div>

          </div>
        `;
      });

      container.innerHTML = html;
      lucide.createIcons();
    }
  </script>


</body></html>

parts.text:
Build me an app that shows all open pull requests across our repos
as a review queue, sorted by how long they’ve been waiting.
Your [PR Review Queue](/a/fa2d8c82-c417-46fc-af3c-64904d5fc16b) is ready, providing an interactive review queue of open pull requests sorted by waiting time.

enhancement.description: Open GitHub pull requests across all repositories, sorted by how long they've been waiting for review.
enhancement.prompt: Build me an app that connects to GitHub and displays all our open pull requests as a unified review queue, sorted by how long they've been waiting so we can easily see what needs attention first.
enhancement.response:
I have built the PR Review Queue app to help you easily manage and prioritize open pull requests.

- Retrieves live pull request data across your repositories using secure GitHub integration.
- Sorts the queue automatically by age, placing the longest-waiting PRs right at the top.
- Displays key details for each item, including the repository name, author, and branch status.
- Provides direct links to open and review the pull requests on GitHub instantly.

Just log in with your GitHub account to load your active pull requests and start clearing the queue.
